content: Follistatin-related protein 1 (FSTL1) is a protein encoded by the FSTL1 gene in humans. This protein shares structural similarities with follistatin, a known binding protein for bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP-4). FSTL1 specifically binds to BMP-4 and transforming growth factor-beta 1 (TGF-β1), but it does not interact with Activin A. The protein structure of FSTL1 includes several distinct domains: an FS module, which is a follistatin-like sequence containing 10 conserved cysteine residues; a Kazal-type serine protease inhibitor domain; two EF-hand domains; and a Von Willebrand factor type C domain. FSTL1 plays a critical role in various developmental processes. It is involved in the development of the lungs, ureters, central nervous system, and skeletal system. In the context of rheumatoid arthritis, FSTL1 is believed to act as an autoantigen. It has been shown to upregulate proinflammatory mediators that are crucial in the pathogenesis of arthritis. Furthermore, serum levels of FSTL1 have been found to correlate with the severity of arthritis, suggesting its potential as a biomarker for disease progression. FSTL1 also appears to have significant cardioprotective properties. Muscle-derived FSTL1 plays a role in vascular remodeling following injury. Additionally, FSTL1 has demonstrated therapeutic potential in promoting cardiac regeneration after myocardial infarction. In studies involving mice and pigs, treatment with FSTL1 after myocardial infarction led to progressive restoration of heart function. This effect is thought to be mediated, at least in part, by stimulating the replication of heart muscle cells, which typically do not divide under normal conditions.
